facts.claim: Claywater Station sells goods and services to travellers.
A traveller can rest safely at Claywater Station.
Claywater Station offers services to travellers.
Claywater Station gives shelter for the night.
Claywater Station is a mixed village where the road crosses the Claywater ford.
An Imperial well and station house stand on one bank of the ford.
An Argonian landing stands on the other bank.
The landing is older than the station.
Argonian polers worked the ford before the Imperials dug the well.
A poler's canoe lies pulled up on the bank.
The ford is shallow and stony, so a walker can wade it and a cart cannot.
Two communities share the village because neither can hold the other's half.
The Imperial-built well is failing.
The Argonian half of the village will not help to repair the well in stone.
The ford divides the station half from the landing half. The two halves face each other over the water.
Low round mud huts stand on the landing bank.
The mud half of the village was replastered last year.
A bucket stands by the well.
Two languages are spoken, one from each bank.
The village is the road's water point at the ford.
A plank ferry carries carts across the ford.
The well and the landing charge travellers separately for the same stop.
The station house roof shows first to an arriving traveller.
Across the ford the huts sit low by the water.
The station half uses Imperial timber framing and well masonry.
The landing half uses Argonian mud walls and thatch.
The mood is neighbourly and wary.
The station half is wet stone grey and weathered timber.
The landing half is mud brown and thatch gold.
The two halves do not share a colour.
The village would become one community or two villages within a generation.
